reply_text:
I found two dated statements from 2016. Both are in one essay LeCun wrote in French for his Collège de France chair, and neither gives a firm date. Each names a span of time and hedges it.

**Candidates:**

- **How long until truly intelligent machines.** He wrote that without solving unsupervised learning we will not have truly intelligent machines, and that solving it could take "many years or several decades." In the next breath he admits nobody knows.
- **Aligning machine values.** He wrote that "in a few decades," when we can perhaps think about designing truly intelligent machines, we will have to work out how to align their values with human morals.

**Where they come from.** The essay is titled "Les Enjeux de la Recherche en Intelligence Artificielle" and carries his name and chair title on every page. It is printed inside the Collège de France press kit for his 4 February 2016 inaugural lecture. The kit is stamped "Février 2016" on the cover and "Janvier 2016" on the inner pages, so I give the date as January–February 2016. The site returned the PDF as raw data, so I pulled the text out with a PDF reader and copied it exactly, keeping the original French and its one typo ("Elle ne seront"). The quotes in the JSON are in French; the English above is my own translation.

**Left out:**

- **Quora Q&A, 28 July 2016.** He answered "What are the likely AI advancements in the next 5 to 10 years?", but the part I could read gives no date. I saw it only as a quote on a third-party blog, because the Quora pages refused to open. His answer on the singularity "within the next century" also has no date in his own words.
- **AlphaGo, March 2016.** His Facebook posts reached me only through news reports, and nothing I saw gave a date.
- **Belongs to 2017, not 2016.** The MIT Technology Review interview is from 9 March 2017, and the "A Path to AI" slides were uploaded in January 2017. I didn't open either one.

I used 8 of the 12 searches and all 6 page openings; three of the openings were blocked Quora pages.
